title: The Detention of the quarry
premise: Tamsin Galloway transfers to Marrow Creek High, a school built atop the flooded quarry where the town's founding families once 'paid the water' — an annual ritual of sacrifice disguised as a scholarship tradition. When their only friend, Priya, vanishes leaving behind a ring of old brass keys, Tamsin discovers the keys open sealed maintenance tunnels beneath the school and that Priya had uncovered the truth: the town's prosperity is sustained by a covenant that demands a life every generation. As the solstice deadline approaches, Tamsin must decide whether to break the covenant and doom the town's economy, or let the water take someone else — and learns the covenant's true keeper is the beloved principal who once saved Tamsin's own mother. In the end, Tasmis floods the covenant archive, offering the water a truth instead of a life: the town survives poorer but free, and Priya is pulled from the rising dark on the final night.
about_author: Felix Nakamura is a former substitute teacher who spent three years in a rust-belt mill town where every civic monument seemed to hide a debt. They write young adult stories about kids who inherit problems older than they are.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Arriving mid-semester at Marrow Creek High, Tamsin maps the social terrain like a survival exercise: who to avoid, which stairwell is quiet, why the east wing smells of lake water. Establishes their rules of invisibility and the first crack in them — Priya, who talks to them anyway. Emotional beat: wary loneliness beginning to loosen.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Nobody Applies For
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya explains the Galloway Fund, the town's founding scholarship that 'chooses' one senior each year — always a kid whose family is struggling. She's joking about it, mostly, but her research notebook says otherwise. Tamsin laughs it off. Emotional beat: friendship cemented over shared skepticism.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A normal week rendered in precise detail — until Tamsin notices the trophy case: every 'chosen' student photographed by the quarry, decades of smiling faces, several who later 'moved away.' Priya stops joking. Emotional beat: unease creeping through routine.

chapters.title: Keys on the Concrete
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya misses first period, then the day, then doesn't answer. In Priya's locker, left deliberately visible, is a ring of seven brass keys and a note in Priya's handwriting: 'COUNT THEM. DON'T TELL THE OFFICE.' Police call it a runaway. Tamsin knows better. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Seven Doors
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, night sections. Testing the keys one by one through the school after hours: a boiler room, a records annex, and finally a hatch behind the gym that opens onto quarry tunnels flooded to the old waterline. In the last room, Priya's research, half-finished. Emotional beat: dread and wonder in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Water Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The archive reveals the covenant: in 1898 the founding families drowned the quarry works and 'gave the water a keeper,' and every generation since, the Fund selects a student who vanishes — and the town thrives. Tamsin's own name is on the current page. Emotional beat: the horror of being already written into something.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin investigates the vanished 'chosen' students of past decades and finds them alive — scattered, changed, sworn to silence, some grateful. One old woman tells them: 'It isn't murder, child. It's a trade, and the town always gets the better half.' Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: The Principal's Kindness
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Principal Voss — who waived Tamsin's fees, who knew their mother — begins gently steering Tamsin toward accepting the Fund 'honor.' Tamsin plays along while realizing Voss is the covenant's keeper. Emotional beat: the sick discovery that care and capture can wear the same face.

chapters.title: Mother's Debt
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Tamsin's POV. Tamsin learns their mother was a chosen student who fled twenty years ago, and that her running is why the water 'is owed twice.' The family's bad luck, the eviction, the move — all downstream of the covenant. Emotional beat: inherited guilt made concrete.

chapters.title: Ally in the Tunnels
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A former 'chosen' student, Dez, still lives in town and agrees to help — reluctantly, because he tried to break the covenant once and his brother paid for it. He teaches Tamsin the tunnels and the one rule: the water must be offered something willingly given. Emotional beat: cautious alliance.

chapters.title: Countdown at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, fragmented and waterlogged. Interludes of Priya alive in a boathouse beneath the quarry, kept by the water itself, lucid but fading — the covenant holding her until solstice. She leaves coded messages in the damp. Emotional beat: terror tempered by stubborn hope.

chapters.title: The Founders' Descendants
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confronts the five remaining founding families at a gala for the Fund. They are not villains; they are tired custodians who genuinely believe the trade built every good thing in Marrow Creek. One, quietly, slips Tamsin a key — the eighth. Emotional beat: sympathy for the complicit.

chapters.title: What the Water Wants
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez explains the mechanics: the covenant isn't a demon but a bargain with the aquifer itself, and it has grown greedy — it now takes the town's memories of the taken, which is why no one grieves. Priya's parents can't even describe her face. Emotional beat: grief for a grief that's been stolen.

chapters.title: The Offer They Expect
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Voss formally offers Tamsin the Fund: full ride, family debts erased, mother's record cleaned — in exchange for walking into the water at solstice. Tamsin says yes, and means to betray them, and hates how tempting the deal truly is. Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Eighth Key
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The eighth key opens the covenant's heart: the original 1898 contract, signed in blood and quarry water, with an amendment clause the founders buried — the bargain can be renegotiated if 'a truth is given freely that outweighs a life.' Nobody has ever dared try. Emotional beat: a door cracking open.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Hatch
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dez's brother — alive, and a covenant enforcer — catches Tamsin copying the contract. Voss's kindness curdles; Tamsin is confined to 'protective custody' until solstice, and the eighth key is confiscated. Emotional beat: the plan collapsing, isolation total.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The town decorates for the Founders' Vigil, festive and oblivious. Tamsin, guarded in the school, uses the one thing guards can't confiscate: they memorized the amendment clause and recite it aloud to the water through the old floor drains — a truth, freely given, spoken into the dark. Emotional beat: defiance with no guarantee.

chapters.title: The Renegotiation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax begins. At midnight the tunnels flood upward and the Vigil becomes a crisis. Tamsin escapes custody through the boiler room, races to the contract chamber, and offers the water the founders' greatest secret: that they falsified the 1898 ledger and the covenant has been fed by a lie for a century. The water must choose: the truth or a life. Emotional beat: terrifying, exhilarating stakes.

chapters.title: What Tamsin Gave the Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. The water takes the truth — the town's false prosperity story dissolves, the Fund's money evaporates into debt, and the quarry begins to drain, exposing a century of bones and names. Priya surfaces in the old works, alive. Voss, freed from her role, weeps. Emotional beat: catharsis at real cost.

chapters.title: A Poorer Town
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Aftermath: Marrow Creek reels as the covenant's subsidy dies — businesses close, the school faces consolidation — but people begin remembering the taken, and the first true funerals in a century are held. Some residents hate Tamsin. Some finally grieve. Emotional beat: bittersweet reckoning.

chapters.title: Priya, Counting Keys
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recovers slowly, her memories of the water intact and hers. She and Tamsin return the seven keys to the drained quarry, then keep the eighth — the amendment key — between them. She asks Tamsin why they did it. Tamsin says, 'You counted them first.' Emotional beat: friendship reforged in daylight.

chapters.title: The Quarry, Open Air
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. A year later: the quarry is a public park under renovation, the school's east wing condemned and honest about what it hid. Tamsin's family stays, poorer and rooted. On the last day of school, Tamsin leaves their locker open — head up, for once. Emotional beat: earned peace, and vigilance.
